summary: WorldEntity's primary live-record registry has no project-owned capacity: unique registrations accumulate without a maximum and count() rescans the full records map. Recommend a bounded follow-up after active WorldEntity closure rather than widening PR #293 in review.
evidence: At active PR #293 exact head c301d8403d3c1b93ee3b2988f80e9d1e689eb33d, createRegistry(config) exposes duplicateDiagnosticCapacity only; there is no maxRegisteredEntities/live-record budget.

Registry:register owns then inserts every unique WorldEntityId into records with no capacity rejection, so a long-lived authority can retain arbitrarily many live records subject only to process memory.
Registry:count iterates pairs(self.records) on every call, making the observable count path O(n) as the unbounded map grows.

tests/world_entity_registry_shape.luau covers identity, aliasing, lifecycle, duplicate diagnostics, and diagnostic-capacity boundaries but establishes no maximum live-record budget or at-capacity rejection invariant.

This is distinct from evt-20260811-080710-e08449-worldentity-capacity, which concerns duplicate-diagnostic retention, and from the active persistentState depth/width boundedness work; it concerns cardinality of owned WorldEntity records themselves.
Docs/QUALITY_STANDARD.md requires explicit queue/cache/core-foundation budgets; this is a source-only capacity finding and claims no Studio, physics, or two-client evidence.
